notes.text: Data rate 800 kbit/s.
Bit timing: T0H 220–380 ns, T1H 580 ns–1 µs, T0L/T1L 580 ns–1 µs; reset (frame) low time above 280 µs.
Data order GRB, high bit first.
This revision (V5 chip) needs no external parts, not even capacitors.
VIH is 0.63·VDD (3.15 V at 5 V): a 3.3 V GPIO is above it only in typical conditions, not by the ESP32's guaranteed VOH. Use a 5 V-supplied level shifter (e.g. 74AHCT125) for a 5 V strip.
Older WS2812B revisions specify VIH 0.7·VDD, a reset time above 50 µs and a 100 nF capacitor per LED; this entry follows revision V6.1.
Strip vendors recommend a 300–500 Ω series resistor in the data line and a large capacitor across 5 V at the strip input (Adafruit guidance, not in the Worldsemi datasheet).

notes.text: The only datasheet found is an image-only distributor copy without revision (class B); every value below was read from the page images and is unverified.
LED pins as printed on p. 1: 1 DI, 2 CI, 3 GND, 4 VCC (+5V), 5 CO, 6 DO.
Supply VDD typ 5.0 V, max 5.5 V; absolute maximum supply -0.3 to 6.0 V, inputs VSS-0.3 to VDD+0.3 (p. 3).
VIH min 0.7·VDD (3.5 V at 5 V), VIL max 0.3·VDD (p. 3): at 5 V a 3.3 V GPIO needs a level shifter on DI and CI.
Built-in 20 mA constant-current outputs (p. 1); sink current per channel 22.5/24.5/26.5 mA min/typ/max at VDD 5 V, VOL > 1 V (p. 3); power consumption 0.2 W (max 1 W) per LED (p. 1).

Frame: start frame 32 zero bits, per LED 32 bits (111 + 5-bit global brightness + blue, green, red, MSB first), end frame of 32 one bits (p. 3); the global value scales the current in 31 steps (p. 4).
No maximum clock frequency is given; the example on p. 4 uses 512 kHz.
DotStar strips use APA102 or the SK9822 clone, whose global-brightness handling differs.
